headline: The ledger's REASONING was broken but its CONCLUSION was right. The metric that refuted WF (P/B per unit of ROE) is identically P/E/100, its stated inputs are irreproducible, and four supporting facts are false or stale. Mid-court this looked like a clean reversal. It is not: a KRW 581bn one-time bargain-purchase gain (18.6% of FY25 profit, booked H2-25 and therefore inside the TTM window) and a March-2026 land revaluation supplying ~60bp of the 82bp CET1 improvement together remove the discount. On every consistently constructed basis Woori trades AT or ~1.3% ABOVE peer-consistent value. 'Correctly priced' is the right answer, reached the wrong way.
process_note: The first pass of this court reversed the ledger and scored WF a hold-toward-build at +13.6% edge. It was WRONG. Disconfirming evidence arrived after the initial write-up and flipped the answer back; both decisive facts were re-verified directly against the 20-F and the Rule 802 prospectus before acting (escalate-on-decisive-findings rule). All corrections cut against the position -- the direction of error to trust (asymmetric-error rule).

edge_note: This is FAIR VALUE, not edge. The 4.04% dividend is the return; the +2.9% price component is noise. Scenario base and bull both sit BELOW the entire April Street range (KRW 38,000-47,000, median 43,000) -- the expected posture once the bargain-purchase gain is removed from the earnings base the Street was capitalising.

decisive_findings.title: KRW 581bn of FY2025 profit is a one-time bargain-purchase gain -- DECISIVE
decisive_findings.quote: 'The eight-fold increase in other non-operating income was primarily attributable to a bargain purchase gain of KRW 581 billion that was recognized in 2025, which in turn was attributable to our acquisitions of Tongyang Life Insurance and ABL Life Insurance in July 2025.'
decisive_findings.authority: Woori 20-F FY2025, filed 2026-04-22, MD&A 'Other Non-Operating Income (Expenses)' -- READ DIRECTLY
decisive_findings.corroboration: Effective tax rate fell to 21.1% in 2025 from 24.9% -- consistent with a largely non-taxable IFRS 3 gain.
decisive_findings.why_it_bites: The deals closed JULY 2025, so the gain sits in H2-2025 -- exactly the half inside the trailing-twelve-month window. Any screen showing Woori at 7.7x trailing earnings is capitalising an acquisition-accounting entry. The clean number is 9.4x, DEARER than Shinhan (9.1x) and Hana (8.9x) on the lowest ROE of the four.

decisive_findings.title: Most of the CET1 improvement is a land revaluation whose surplus is not distributable
decisive_findings.quote: 'as of March 31, 2026, the Wholly-Owning Company conducted an asset revaluation of its property and equipment. However, such revaluation is an accounting effect that does not involve any cash inflow, and capital ratios may be affected by future changes in asset values and market conditions.'
decisive_findings.authority: Form CB / Rule 802 prospectus 2026-07-16, Basel-III capital section -- READ DIRECTLY
decisive_findings.effect: CET1 12.89% (4Q25) -> 13.60% (1Q26) -> 13.71% (2Q26) = +82bp, of which ~60bp is the revaluation (magnitude agent-sourced from the H1-26 Fact Book; existence/timing CONFIRMED primary). The revaluation surplus is NOT DISTRIBUTABLE under the Korean Commercial Code. ORGANIC CET1 ~= 13.1% -- barely over the 13.0% line and BELOW the 13.2% maintenance target.
decisive_findings.why_it_bites: This guts the strongest bull leg. Woori's Dec-2024 value-up plan maps year-end CET1 >=13.0% to ~50% total shareholder return (vs 36.8% delivered FY25). The ladder may still trigger MECHANICALLY -- but the capital that pushed CET1 over the line cannot fund the buyback the ladder promises. Catalyst probability cut 0.75 -> 0.55.

peer_comparison._basis: annualized-H1-2026 reported ROE against LIKE-FOR-LIKE EX-HYBRID P/B. Methodology trap handled: KB and Shinhan publish BVPS INCLUDING hybrid/AT1; Hana and Woori EXCLUDING. On published numbers Shinhan (0.81x) screens cheaper than Hana (0.82x); restated like-for-like the ranking FLIPS.
peer_comparison.woori_rank: SECOND-MOST EXPENSIVE of the four per unit of delivered ROE (0.0767 vs median 0.0759)
peer_comparison.ruling: The ledger's METRIC is refuted, its NUMBERS are irreproducible, and FOUR of its supporting facts are wrong -- but its CONCLUSION ('just correctly priced') is CORRECT, and this court confirms it on a full four-name peer set with a like-for-like book basis and acquisition accounting removed. Woori is not a mispriced laggard; it is the sector's weakest operator, priced accordingly.

ledger_facts_refuted: 'P/B per unit of delivered ROE = 0.060 vs 0.0485, KB 24% better paid' -- METRIC DEGENERATE (P/B/ROE is identically P/E/100, because P/B == ROE x P/E) and INPUTS IRREPRODUCIBLE (0.0485 would require KB to trade at 4.85x earnings, which it never has)

'no securities arm' -- REFUTED: Woori operates banking, insurance, credit card, capital finance, financial investment (securities), asset management and real-estate trust (Form CB business description); Woori Investment & Securities profit +2.3x (Seoul Economic Daily 2026-08-02)
'payout 31.8%' -- UNDERSTATED: FY25 total shareholder return 36.8% (32.0% dividend + 4.8% buyback), 40.0% incl. tax-exempt effect
'CET1 ~100bp thinner (caps buybacks)' -- REFUTED on the headline: 13.71% vs KB 13.74 / Shinhan 13.43 / Hana 13.21 = PARITY (though ~60bp is a non-distributable revaluation -- see decisive finding 2)
'cancellation +33%/yr' -- UNDERSTATED: FY26 buyback KRW 350bn vs FY25 KRW 150bn = +133.3%; apparently a transcription error
what_survives_in_wf_favour: Buyback accretion asymmetry is REAL and durable: Woori's Jul tranche (0.667% of shares at 0.69x book) is +0.21% ACCRETIVE to BVPS; KB's (1.139% at 1.06x) is -0.15% DILUTIVE. Woori's own prospectus: 'the benefits of share cancellations are maximized when PBR is below 1.0x.' BUT Woori deploys KRW 350bn against KB's KRW 3.7trn plan -- the better mechanism at one-tenth the scale is not a thesis.

Dividend yield 4.14% vs KB 2.71%, with genuine tax-exempt dividend capacity (KRW 6.3trn, first Korean financial holdco; Q2-26 dividend paid from capital reserve, non-taxable IN KOREA). US-holder treaty benefit NOT verified -- do not underwrite.
Still the 2026 laggard (+23% YTD vs peers +37-40%) -- optionality if the Korea re-rate broadens.

The regulatory overhang is SMALLER than the ledger implied -- which is BAD for the thesis: it removes governance as the explanation for the 0.69x vs 1.06x book gap, leaving only the ROE gap, and an ROE discount closes only by earning more.

edge_explainer: The ledger killed WF with a metric that is algebraically degenerate -- P/B per unit of ROE is identically P/E divided by 100 -- whose stated inputs (0.060 vs 0.0485) cannot be reproduced from any real prices, and which rested on four facts that are false or stale: Woori DOES have a securities arm, FY25 shareholder return was 36.8% not 31.8%, CET1 is at PARITY with the peer group (13.71% vs KB 13.74 / Shinhan 13.43 / Hana 13.21), and the buyback grew +133% not +33%. Fixing all of that made WF look cheap. It is not. Two verified facts remove the discount. First, KRW 581bn of FY2025 profit -- 18.6% of the total -- is a one-time IFRS 3 bargain-purchase gain from the July-2025 Tongyang/ABL acquisitions (20-F MD&A, read directly), and because the deals closed in July it sits inside the trailing-twelve-month window: strip it and the headline 7.7x trailing P/E becomes 9.4x, DEARER than Shinhan at 9.1x and Hana at 8.9x, on the LOWEST ROE of the four. Second, roughly 60bp of the 82bp CET1 improvement that appeared to arm Woori's >=13% shareholder-return ladder is a March-2026 land revaluation whose surplus is NOT distributable (Form CB, read directly); organic CET1 is ~13.1%, below the 13.2% maintenance target, so the ladder can trigger on paper without the cash to honour it. On a like-for-like ex-hybrid book basis -- and the four banks split on whether BVPS includes hybrid capital, a trap that reverses the Shinhan/Hana ranking -- Woori prices at 0.0767 of book per point of ROE against a sector median of 0.0759: the SECOND-MOST expensive of the four, ~1.3% ABOVE peer-consistent value, while earning the lowest ROE (9.0%), growing profit the slowest (+3.7% vs +13.1%/+13.3%) and returning the least capital (36.8% vs 46.8-52.4%). Even the marketed 'recurring ROE 10.3%' that clears its own >=10% target is an add-back of a KRW 183bn early-retirement charge that recurs annually; restore it and recurring ROE is ~9.3%, still below the 10.93% cost of equity. The regulatory overhang turns out to be SMALLER than the record implied -- indictments only, no institutional sanction, the FSC approved both insurer deals while the probe was live -- which is bad news, because it removes governance as the explanation for the 0.69x vs 1.06x book gap and leaves only the ROE gap, and an ROE discount closes by earning more, not by a catalyst. What survives is a carry position: 4.04% yield, buybacks that accrete book instead of burning it (+0.21% vs KB's -0.15%), and laggard optionality (+23% YTD vs +37-40%), against a 1.19% share listing on 2026-08-31 and a price +26% off a 44-day-old low. So: hold as carry, retire the build, flag the rotate to Shinhan (0.0711 of book per point of ROE, the sector's best, 50.2% TSR already delivered) for a tax-efficient window, and rest the exit ladder through the listing. E[FV] $71.80 against $69.80 -- fair value, not edge.
